author: Codex documentation author; corrections by DOC-029 source-review author agent (analysis-standin)

prerequisites: Disposable lab openlaw-docs-41255c61-analysis-r1 from app commit 3fa407e3, seeded with the fictional Helix data.
AI connector configured by the Administrator to the local OpenAI-compatible stand-in (provider-standin.mjs) on the lab network; known fictional paper and answers.
Contract type with three prompted Fields and one live Counterparty created by the Administrator through the API.
scenarios.expected: Evidence is tied to the chosen Document Version; confirming one value does not clear unrelated markers. Disabled connector, failed extraction, changed source, and stale evidence have the documented states. C43 separately verifies real provider setup.
scenarios.actual: 17 recorded steps passed for Nadia Haddad (Legal Team Member). Refusals: no primary Document, failed extraction (text state failed), and a disabled connector with no run or markers (card absent, no Run analysis in Contract actions, 409). An automatic run on the first primary PDF showed Running… then Completed … on Version 1 with doc029-standin-model without a reload; rows read Written, Kept (duplicate expiry milestone), Unmatched (unknown Counterparty, nothing linked), Invalid and Unsupported with their quotes; a typed draft on another Contract stayed in its control when the card updated. Unverified values showed the indicator, the purple AI border and evidence sparkles; a sparkle opened Version 1 in the same-page doc panel with the quote marked; the Key date and derived notice deadline were listed before confirmation. Confirm cleared only its marker; a Field edit cleared its marker; a Key date note-only edit kept the marker and an event change cleared it; Confirm all showed with several markers; History recorded the confirmation. Mark as executed copy on Version 1 ran on Version 1; a newer Version started no run and sent nothing to the provider; Run analysis and the earlier evidence still used Version 1. Pinning Version 2 ran on Version 2 while Daniel Okafor edited a prompted Field: the unverified expiry was replaced, confirmed, edited and concurrently edited values were Kept with different returned answers, the matching live Counterparty was linked, and a new milestone was written. Remove date cleared its marker and a later run did not add it again; a cleared Field stayed empty. A malformed provider reply ended Failed … on Version 2 with the model and reason and changed nothing; the next run completed. A supporting Document with ready text started no run. Ended removed Run analysis (409) but Confirm worked; archived removed Confirm (409) until Restore; with the connector disabled the card and markers stayed and Confirm all cleared them without changing values. A Business User on the team landed on /portal and was refused run and confirm (403). With Fill Contract Fields after conversion on, a converted Contract read Filling…, then Request-context Analysis failed with the Contract still created, then Retry Request-context Analysis completed.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the technical reviewer. It is not a human user study and not the feature owner's approval.
Browser contexts were 1440x1000 CSS px in the default theme. No narrow layout, other theme, keyboard-only or assistive technology check was made.

Prerequisite records were made through the lab API by the acting role or the Administrator: Contract types and Fields, Contracts, uploads of Documents and Versions, Document restore, and Business User team membership. Each is listed in the walkthrough setup notes.

The first three full runs had failures from harness faults or transient page stalls on a loaded host. Their logs are kept as walkthrough-r1-attempt1.json to attempt3.json. The recorded run walkthrough-r1.json passed every step on the same article bytes and build.
The walkthrough ran in a disposable lab, openlaw-docs-41255c61-analysis-r1, built from the committed app source by scripts/documentation/lab.mjs. The lab was destroyed after the run.

C21 used a declared local OpenAI-compatible stand-in with fictional paper and known answers. It verifies OpenLaw's workflow handling, not real provider setup, consent or model quality, and it does not satisfy C43. No external provider traffic occurred.
A retryable provider outage (HTTP 429 or 5xx) was not exercised; the terminal malformed-reply failure was.

Request-context Analysis was checked for filling, failure, Retry Request-context Analysis and completion only. The Request had no attachment, so a promoted Document Version, partial-source warnings, conflicts, restricted or Confidential source exclusion, and switching the setting off were not exercised. The run wrote no value: its cited Counterparty was Unmatched.
An unavailable citation (removed, edited or inaccessible source) was not exercised.
The Ended stage was set through the Contract API by the acting role; archive used Contract actions and restore used the API.
Observation, not an article failure: the Invalid effective date answer 2027-02-30 is displayed in its result row as Mar 2, 2027 while nothing is saved.

compatibilityReview.summary: I inspected the 3fa407e3..57e77e38 app and message diff, and it changes no Analysis, AI analysis card, Key dates or Contract record file and no string this article quotes. I replayed the round 1 V-C21 walkthrough, with Request-context Analysis, on lab analysis-r2 with the local provider stand-in, and all 34 steps passed for the Administrator and the Legal Team Member.
